cells.tense: Right now the choosing is steady, and you stand with what you chose.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: This week, hold the shared decision the two of you already made the first time it gets questioned — one conversation, no drifting off it.
cells.core:
A joining that holds gets its strength from you keeping a direction once it's real. Two people talk and something gets chosen, and you don't wander off it two days later because the mood turned. That steadiness is what the other person is standing on, and it's why a thing you build with someone finishes instead of dissolving. Finishing isn't the loud part. It's the part where you stay pointed and the work is allowed to close.

Take the decision you and another person already made together. This week, keep it when it's tested. If someone wants it done a different way, if it's easier to quietly let it slide, hold the heading anyway. Not a fight. Just no drifting. You'll find out fast which parts of it you actually meant, and the other person will find out too.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold a chosen direction when the room starts pulling.
cells.verb: meeting what you meant to meet and finishing it so it can leave your hands
cells.place: the doorway where what you built together is complete and you are already half turned toward what comes next

cells.tense: You'll be pushing what you built with someone toward a finish line it hasn't reached.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Find a piece of what the two of you built that's already finished and good, then leave it untouched for a week.
cells.core:
The direction holds, and there's real force behind it now. What's coming out is a hurry. You've been seeing the finished version of whatever you're building with someone — them already caught up, the thing already done — and the gap between that and today starts to feel like a problem that needs correcting tonight. So you push, or you quietly adjust them, and what they get is the plan instead of you.

Part of the good thing is already here. Look at it — the shared thing, the person, whatever you two made — and find one piece that's finished and fine. Then don't touch it. Not this week. Let it be done and good while you do other things. Pleasure shows up in a result that's allowed to stand; a result you keep editing gives you nothing to enjoy and someone else nothing to live in.

cells.tense: The two streams met once, and you've been standing back at that doorway since.
cells.act: let several things be true and act on one
cells.ask: Put three true things you can see about a joining that matters onto paper, leave all three standing, then act on the first.
cells.core:
You can read a situation with real accuracy — a person, a partnership, what's actually going on between two people — and near the joins in your own life you stop reading. The picture gets flattened. It's either this or that, mine or theirs, it worked or it didn't. Standing there, one truth at a time, you can't see the finished thing whole long enough to let it be finished.

Take some paper and put down three things you can honestly see about a joining that matters to you. All three, even where they argue. Then pick one and act on it today. Just one — you're not resolving anything. Holding three things at once is what lets a thing close. You can do that part. You've been doing the flatter version with your eyes open.

cells.tense: You're already steering what you built with someone, and the account of it leaves your hand out.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: Walk through the route you found in what the two of you are building — what you tried, what you dropped, where the gap opened — and leave the shrugging out.
cells.core:
There's a passage through whatever you and someone else are making together, and you found it. You know the turns. When the two of you talk about how it's going, the finding isn't in the version you tell — it's luck, it worked out, the other person brought it up first. The path is doing its job. Your hand on it isn't in the account.

Show somebody the route. Not a speech, just the way you got from the stuck part to here — what you tried, what you dropped, where the gap opened. Leave the shrugging out of it. Saying it plainly is what makes it yours to know, and the person hearing it is the one who needs it next, walking the same stretch. You had the route before anyone confirmed you did.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a genuine connection is currently being chosen and completed in this person's life; the record shows the capacity, not the event. A reader could reasonably say the two streams have already met and the choosing happened long ago, and the ask still holds if my read is wrong, because tending what a joining actually produced teaches the person something about their own share in it either way. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is the one about two becoming one flow; I catch myself wanting to say it, so the cells say what the person does instead.
